title: Paul Graham: why founders should go to Silicon Valley, then come back
summary: Graham argues ambitious founders should spend time in the world's startup center for its peer density, serendipitous meetings, speed, investor competition and pay-it-forward culture. He says the best way to help Stockholm thrive is to go to Silicon Valley (ideally via YC) and then return, bringing back better startups, money and culture.

principles.text: Go to the center of your field: you get the best peers, and the talent pool is both better and bigger there.
principles.quote: What exactly do you get when you move to the big center? Um the answer to that question is always the same, too. You get the best peers.

principles.text: Serendipitous meetings are enormously valuable, and big centers produce far more of them.
principles.quote: if you're working on something ambitious, there's nothing in the world that's better than serendipitous meetings with people who are working on the same stuff.

principles.text: Silicon Valley investor competition forces fast decisions, and the speed does not hurt returns.
principles.quote: Silicon Valley investors get better returns than European investors despite having to decide so quickly.

principles.text: Seeing top founders up close turns an impossible goal into a hard, definite one, which is ideal for ambitious people.
principles.quote: it no longer seems an impossible goal, just a hard one. And for an ambitious person, there is nothing better than a high but definite threshold.

principles.text: Silicon Valley's culture of helping people without keeping score lets favors scale, and it will make you more helpful too.
principles.quote: You just like do favors left and right and don't even keep track of whether you're ahead or behind.

principles.text: Go to the hub for a while, then return home: you improve your startup, bring money back and import startup culture.
principles.quote: You make your own startup better, so the average quality of startups here is increased. You're probably going to bring money back with you from Silicon Valley investors.
